performance_interpretation: No profiler counter, pipeline, or instruction evidence exists for this round: all six msprof collections (four workloads, then a single retry of the two key workloads) returned status=failed with an empty artifacts list and the identical error 'msprof base collection exited successfully without profile completion marker'. The service still declares profiler=msprof with levels metrics/instruction and capabilities performance_counters, pipeline_utilization, kernel_profile, instruction_listing, so this is a collection failure on the target, not a declaration that profiling is unsupported. Interpretation below therefore rests only on the authoritative get_profile_context eval numbers and is explicitly not profiler-verified. The round-2 eval splits the twelve timing workloads into two distinct regimes. (a) NINE LAUNCH-FLOOR WORKLOADS, 1024 to 1048576 elements across fp16/bf16/fp32 (timing-0,1,2,4,5,6,8,9,10): candidate latency is 11.5-13.1 us and reference 8.9-11.0 us, i.e. a candidate floor near 11.5-13.1 us that is essentially flat over a 1024x input-size range while the reference still moves with size. A candidate latency that does not track input size over three orders of magnitude is consistent with host-side cost dominating, which is directionally the frozen hypothesis (nine of twelve host-launch bound), but no device-task timing was obtained this round to confirm how much of that floor is the compiled launch versus the wrapper prelude. The round-2 prelude rewrite did move seven of these nine down by 0.65-2.32 us (timing-4 -2.32 us, timing-5 -1.91 us, timing-6 -1.80 us, timing-10 -1.20 us, timing-8 -1.08 us, timing-0 -1.08 us, timing-2 -1.00 us), which is consistent with removing Python work from the call path. (b) THREE LARGE WORKLOADS AT numel=16777216 (4096x4096), all 512 programs under BLOCK_MAX=32768: fp16 36.01 us (0.4403), bf16 38.09 us (0.6654), fp32 53.08 us (0.4908) against references 15.85, 25.34 and 26.05 us. Their latency is 2.3-3.0x the launch floor and scales with bytes per element (fp16 36.0 < bf16 38.1 < fp32 53.1 at identical element count), so a host-side prelude cannot explain a 20-27 us gap; the limiting work is on the device path. These three cases carry the worst speedups and are the only place where a large geo_mean gain is available: closing fp16 and fp32 to reference parity alone would be worth roughly +7% and +6% on geo_mean respectively. One anomaly is unexplained by the round-2 diff: timing-11 (fp32 4096x4096) moved from 38.92 us to 53.08 us (+14.16 us, +36.4%) although the change touched only the host prelude and left kernel, tile and grid identical, while timing-3 and timing-7 stayed flat to within 0.05%. Either run-to-run variance at that size or an unobserved specialization effect; it must not be attributed to the prelude rewrite without measurement. VERDICT ON THE FROZEN HYPOTHESIS: neither supported nor contradicted. The eval deltas on the nine small workloads are consistent with it and the change produced geo_mean 0.6958 -> 0.7233 (+3.94%), but the compiled-launch share of the ~12 us floor was not measured this round, and the hypothesis says nothing about the three 4096x4096 cases that now dominate the loss.

next_experiment.action_description: Leave the host fast path, the masked path and the strided path exactly as they are, and change only the aligned large-input geometry: for contiguous inputs with numel >= 16777216 (the three 4096x4096 cases), have each program consume K=2 consecutive BLOCK_MAX tiles through a compile-time unrolled loop, halving grid from n//BLOCK to n//(2*BLOCK)=256 while every inner tile keeps its current 32768-element shape, so no single live buffer grows. Use n % (K*BLOCK) == 0 as the guard and fall back to the existing single-tile launch otherwise.
next_experiment.expected_impact: If the 20-27 us gap on the 4096x4096 cases is per-program setup plus fine-grained DMA rather than saturated HBM bandwidth, halving the program count should shorten those three cases measurably (fp16 36.0 us and fp32 53.1 us are the targets) and lift geo_mean above the current 0.7232637007603351. If the large cases are bandwidth-saturated, latency and geo_mean will be flat, which refutes the granularity mechanism and redirects the next trial to the log/convert instruction expansion instead.
next_experiment.risks_and_rollback: One 32768-element tile is already 128 KiB in plus 128 KiB out for fp32 against a 192 KiB UB budget, so the compiler is demonstrably splitting each tile; an added loop can still raise live compilation buffers, spill, or fail to compile (a compile error is a separate, non-performance failure and must be recorded as such). Both the correctness contract and the nine small launch-floor workloads are untouched by construction, but any accidental change to _pick_block or the fast-path key would hit them. Keep a copy of the current main.py before editing; rollback is restoring grid = n//block with a single tile per program and re-running the full eval.
success_criteria: All 24 correctness workloads still PASS at the frozen tolerances (fp16/bf16 rtol=atol=0.015, fp32 rtol=atol=0.0001, matched ratio 1) and the in-place identity is preserved (same storage returned and modified).
Full-eval geo_mean strictly exceeds 0.7232637007603351 (round-2 value) with headline timing computed by the same KGS contract.
The three 4096x4096 cases are each faster than their round-2 latency: fp16 below 0.0360061879665062 ms, bf16 below 0.03808779488491606 ms, fp32 below 0.053081350326048944 ms.

None of the nine launch-floor workloads regresses relative to round 2 by more than measurement noise, and timing-11 is re-measured twice to check whether its +36.4% move was variance before any of it is credited or blamed.
If geo_mean is flat while the large cases are unchanged, record the granularity hypothesis as refuted and do not retry the same geometry with a different K.

open_questions: How much of the flat 11.5-13.1 us floor on the nine small workloads is the compiled launcher versus the remaining Python prelude? Unanswerable without a device-task timing for this exact build.

For the 4096x4096 cases, is the 2.3-3.0x gap to reference caused by DMA granularity (transfer size per MTE2 instruction), by achieved HBM bandwidth, or by log/convert instruction expansion in fp32? A single tile-geometry trial can only falsify the granularity branch.

Why did fp32 4096x4096 move +36.4% while the same-numel fp16 and bf16 cases stayed flat to 0.05%? Needs a repeat measurement, not a code change, to separate variance from a real specialization effect.
Does the pointer-alignment key (numel, data_ptr & 15) ever miss in the benchmark loop, silently routing large cases through the ordinary Triton path? Not observable without the profile artifacts.
